Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Keep the supplied language.", "input": "we are setting up the preview for the north quay archive in the small project room beside the reading desk the room opens at nine no sorry at ten on thursday and i need the first walk through to fit between the morning delivery and the lunch break the collection is mostly harbor records from 1984 through 1996 but there are also a few later maps and two boxes of oral history cassettes please keep the preview focused on the material that staff can explain without opening the storage cases

numbered section begin setup checks first confirm that the collection title reads north quay harbor records and that the date range shows 1984 to 1996 second check that the thumbnails load on the laptop as well as the wall monitor third compare the map legend with the printed 1991 sheet and note any label that is too small fourth check the audio sample button with headphones at the table and keep its volume low enough that it does not distract someone reading nearby fifth leave a blank line in the visitor notes area so the staff can jot down questions during the walk through the list is for the room setup and not a substitute for checking the catalog records

on wednesday afternoon please test the page once with the room lights on and once with the curtains drawn because glare changes the map contrast the west window catches the monitor after about two oclock and the table lamp makes the paper chart easier to read if it is angled toward the wall we should keep both lighting notes with the setup record the screen should not be tilted during the visit because its stand is loose and the facilities team has not looked at it yet

when the staff arrive thursday morning the first job is to check the revised labels against the ledger and mark any uncertain wording for the archivist rather than changing it on the spot after that they can walk through the numbered checks and decide who will explain the map and who will handle questions about the cassettes if a visitor asks whether the harbor boundary was always in the same place the answer should point them to both map versions and explain that the preview is showing two reference documents the final room note should include the time the monitor was tested, the version of the map file, and any label that still needs review", "output": "We are setting up the preview for the North Quay Archive in the small project room beside the reading desk. The room opens at nine—no, sorry, at ten on Thursday, and I need the first walkthrough to fit between the morning delivery and the lunch break. The collection is mostly harbor records from 1984 through 1996, but there are also a few later maps and two boxes of oral history cassettes. Please keep the preview focused on the material that staff can explain without opening the storage cases.

We have one large monitor on the wall and a laptop at the table. The monitor is 27 inches and the laptop screen is 14 inches, so the image and text should be easy to compare from both places. The archive assistant will bring a USB-C adapter and a spare power strip on Wednesday. The cable run from the table to the screen is about 3 meters, and it crosses the doorway, so we should route it along the wall instead of leaving it underfoot. The wall outlet is behind the bookcase and cannot be reached without moving two shelves.

The preview page should open on the harbor collection and show the date range in the first screenful. The configuration key is on its own line here.
preview.show_labels
Please leave that setting enabled while we review the descriptive labels, because the volunteers need to see whether the short names make sense beside the full catalog titles. The thumbnail width can stay at 320 pixels for the first review, and the captions should wrap rather than disappear when a title runs long. Do not treat the date range as a claim that every item is dated; some folders have only an approximate decade written on the wrapper.

The scan list has 46 photographs, 12 folded charts, and 8 cassette sleeves. The photographs are mostly black and white, though six have faded color edges, and one has a handwritten note on the back. The charts need a little more space than the photographs because the scale marks are close to the margins, but the cassette sleeves can use the same card size as the photographs. Please keep the back-of-photo notes in the staff view only, and do not put them in the public caption field.

For the opening screen, I want a small map showing the three harbor districts and a short note that explains the names used in the old ledger. The map is a working reference, not a claim that the district borders stayed fixed through the whole date range. We have a printed copy from 1991 and a digital redraw made last winter, and both should be available in the preview. The redraw uses a different shade for the eastern boundary, so give it a legend that can be read on the wall monitor.

Numbered section: Setup checks.
1. First, confirm that the collection title reads North Quay Harbor Records and that the date range shows 1984 to 1996.
2. Second, check that the thumbnails load on the laptop as well as the wall monitor.
3. Third, compare the map legend with the printed 1991 sheet and note any label that is too small.
4. Fourth, check the audio sample button with headphones at the table and keep its volume low enough that it does not distract someone reading nearby.
5. Fifth, leave a blank line in the visitor notes area so the staff can jot down questions during the walkthrough.
The list is for the room setup and not a substitute for checking the catalog records.

If the rights staff have not confirmed the cassette excerpt by Wednesday afternoon, then keep the audio sample button hidden for the Thursday preview and use the sleeve image instead. If they confirm it in time, we can include the excerpt, but keep it to the first 18 seconds because the following section names a private donor. Please do not describe the excerpt as cleared before that confirmation arrives. The collection manager said, “The donor note is still being checked,” and asked us to avoid guessing about the speaker.

The visitor notes should have space for six short entries, and the paper form should remain beside the laptop rather than on the monitor table, so people do not block the map while writing. We have a blue pencil cup, three clipboards, and a stack of twelve forms in the cabinet by the door. If the forms run low during the preview, the assistant can make another copy from the shared folder, but there is no need to print them in advance. The form asks for a name only if the visitor wants a reply.

On Wednesday afternoon, please test the page once with the room lights on and once with the curtains drawn, because glare changes the map contrast. The west window catches the monitor after about two o’clock, and the table lamp makes the paper chart easier to read if it is angled toward the wall. We should keep both lighting notes with the setup record. The screen should not be tilted during the visit because its stand is loose, and the facilities team has not looked at it yet.

When the staff arrive Thursday morning, the first job is to check the revised labels against the ledger and mark any uncertain wording for the archivist rather than changing it on the spot. After that, they can walk through the numbered checks and decide who will explain the map and who will handle questions about the cassettes. If a visitor asks whether the harbor boundary was always in the same place, the answer should point them to both map versions and explain that the preview is showing two reference documents. The final room note should include the time the monitor was tested, the version of the map file, and any label that still needs review."}]
